title: Study evaluating various parameters in the blood and tissue of patients with endocrine orbitopathy in Graves' disease. An approach to personalized medicine.
summary:
Endocrine orbitopathy is a disease closely related to Graves' disease. It is characterized by chronic inflammation, which leads to an increase in fatty tissue around the eye and the eye muscles. The classic clinical picture includes (unilateral or bilateral) protrusion of the eyes to varying degrees, eye movement disorders with double vision, lubrication disorders, and signs of inflammation. Subjective symptoms include a feeling of pressure, pain when moving the eyes, and increased sensitivity to light and a foreign body sensation due to the lubrication disorder. The optic nerve may also be damaged, especially if the symptoms are left untreated. 
However, it is known that there is a direct causal relationship between the course of thyroid disease and the disease, both in terms of its progression over time and its severity. Depending on its severity, the disease is treated with medication or surgery. Nevertheless, there is still no causal therapy available to primarily prevent consequential damage in the eye socket or  explain why endocrine orbitopathy exhibits such pronounced clinical variability.  The aim of this project is to transfer our findings from the mouse model to the clinic, but also to evaluate findings from the clinic in the mouse model.
